scope: Distinct equal numeric geometry through binary project encoding and restore
before: Content-only chunk deduplication merged distinct equal arrays; four ownership checks failed when made mandatory.
change: Store distinct numeric arrays in distinct existing-format chunks, reuse a chunk for repeated references to the same array, and lend a cached shared buffer to at most one chunk per decode. Keep the first matching shared chunk stable when remembering a batch.
compatibility: No binary version change. Legacy content-deduplicated files remain readable but cannot recover distinctions absent from their stored references. Older readers may still merge equal chunks when borrowing cached data.
tradeoff: Files may be larger when they contain distinct numeric arrays with equal contents.

broadMcpBrowserSmoke.initialFailure: Alignment companion checkbox was covered by the surrounding properties panels.

limitations: Older content-deduplicated files do not encode whether equal arrays were distinct.
Two expected failures remain for mutation of borrowed ordinary arrays after or during numeric-reuse restore.
The large PLY-3 run used public MCP import without downloading the artifact or reopening through the GUI; a single passing run near the cap does not establish resource reliability.
Broader native parity, dirty-main integration and milestone closure remain open.
